insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA for modeled attribution. This protocol settles at roughly $0.10 per cryptographically verified receipt — a 50–200x cost difference that isn't a feature gap, it's a structural one: the receipt eliminates the attribution problem rather than solving it.

insights.topic: Cookie deprecation leaves no equivalent replacement
insights.insight: Chrome has joined Safari and Firefox in killing cross-site cookies, and device fingerprinting is being progressively blocked by privacy regulation. First-party data is accurate only within a single ecosystem — none of these alternatives produce identity-free, cross-ecosystem, verified purchase signals at scale.

22 active CBSAs now span non-metro corridors from Maine to Arizona, with the Southeast rural corridor activating in force in recent cycles. Urban-biased ad tech platforms have no comparable infrastructure for these populations — the geographic reach here is a structural gap, not a marginal one.

insights.topic: Cross-ecosystem visibility without platform data sharing
insights.insight: Amazon knows what you buy on Amazon; Walmart knows what you buy at Walmart. This protocol accumulates cross-ecosystem purchase data from email receipts — no platform needs to open its silo, and no identity is in the payload. The Nash equilibrium that keeps brand data siloed does not apply here.

125 receipts in the 14-day window are categorized as Unknown, generating $16,785 in GMV at a $134 average basket — the highest of any category. These are real, verified transactions from merchants that fail name resolution, meaning brand-level analysis is systematically undercounting a high-value segment.

insights.topic: Category entropy at record high across three commerce cohorts
insights.insight: Category entropy has reached 3.174 bits — its highest recorded value — with physical retail, digital infrastructure, and DTC merchants (via Shopify) now all flowing through the same signal stream. The basket is diversifying, not concentrating, which means the signal is becoming more useful for cross-category targeting, not less.
